videos.script: Lesson 14 fixed shared state with locks. This lesson is the tools that let you stop writing locks yourself. {{atomic}} An atomic counter does the read, the add and the write as one operation of the processor. Four threads, four million increments, four million on the counter, and no lock anywhere. {{map}} A plain HashMap shared by four threads miscounts, and sometimes worse. A ConcurrentHashMap with merge counts every word. {{queue}} A blocking queue is a handover between threads: one side puts, the other takes, and when the queue is full the producer waits instead of running ahead. {{choose}} And at the end, a table: which collection for which kind of sharing, so that the lock you need is already inside it.
